images.title: Three moves from one roll
images.purpose: Show that the roll +5 and −2 gives three different moves: +3, +7 and −7.
images.composition: One horizontal number line centred, three arrows stacked above it in separate rows with wide spacing.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal number line with 17 evenly spaced ticks from −8 to 8, the 0 tick longer. Three arrows each start at the 0 tick, in three separate rows: a teal #0072B2 arrow right to the 3 tick, an amber #E69F00 arrow right to the 7 tick, and a reddish purple #CC79A7 arrow left to the −7 tick. Exactly 17 ticks, 3 arrows, no overlap.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: One roll gives a choice of moves: +3, +7 or −7.
images.description: A number line with three arrows from 0: teal to +3, amber to +7 and purple to −7, all from the roll +5 and −2.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at each arrow and say which way it moves and how far.

image_decisions.why: The set of moves from one roll is a picture idea; one clean number line carries it.
